texts.li: [lowtech] Salt, dried fish and coils of rope, bound from the coast for the hill towns. The caravan of {FACTION} has carried it all down the long road, and {X_nameDef}, the caravan master, told {A_nameDef} the beasts need a rest and the water barrels need filling, and asked whether they might camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[!lowtech] A convoy of {FACTION}'s long-haul traders has pulled off the road near the colony, its vehicles patched and its canvas gray with dust. {X_nameDef}, who runs it, told {A_nameDef} they're waiting on a part and would like to camp {PLACE} for a few days. They'll trade while they wait.

[ws:toll] The toll has sent {FACTION}'s caravan the long way round, and the long way round goes past the colony. {X_nameDef}, the caravan master, asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE} to rest the animals before the hills.

[their:friend] A caravan of {FACTION} has stopped by the colony, and {X_nameDef}, its master, asked for {A_nameDef} by name: {FACTION} tell the story of what {A_pronoun} once did for them on every road they travel. They'd like to camp {PLACE} for a few days.

[winter] A caravan of {FACTION}, caught by the weather between towns, has turned off the road toward the colony's smoke. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to camp {PLACE} until the beasts are rested and the road is clear.

settled.li: The caravan from {FACTION} has made camp {PLACE}, with the bales stacked into a wall against the wind and a kettle on the fire that never seems to come off.
The caravan's camp is up {PLACE}, with its goods laid out on a table for anyone who wants to look, and a guard on the bales who doesn't seem to sleep.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the caravan's drivers, has walked the long road for eleven years and would like, for once, to stop somewhere. The colony would do, {X_pronoun} says, if the colony will have {X_objective}.
{X_nameDef} from the caravan {PLACE} has been looking at the colony's fields with an expression the others recognize. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether there was a place for {X_objective} here.

farewell.li: The caravan from {FACTION} loaded up before dawn and went on toward the hills, bells ringing on the lead animal. {X_nameDef} promised to stop again next year.
The salt caravan's camp {PLACE} is empty. A few grains of salt still glitter in the dirt where the bales stood.
[!lowtech] The convoy from {FACTION} got its part and its engines running, and was gone by mid-morning in a cloud of exhaust and goodwill.

lines.li: Best price this side of the coast.

helpTexts.li: [goods] {X_nameDef}, the caravan master, set a few things aside from the packs for the colony, by way of thanks for the water and the quiet: {THING}.
[goods] The caravan {PLACE} had more than it could carry over the hills, and {X_nameDef} left the colony some of it rather than throw it away: {THING}.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat up half the night at the caravan's fire while {X_nameDef} told the news of every town between here and the sea. {A_nameDef} came back with a head full of names and roads.
[tales] The caravan's drivers had stories from the far roads, and {A_nameDef} heard most of them twice, told different ways by different drivers.

li.label: Spend an evening at their fire
li.tip: The colony goes over to the caravan's fire this evening to swap stories and news from the road. Recreation for whoever comes; the caravan warms to the colony.

outcomes.li: The colony is going over to the caravan's fire this evening. {X_nameDef} has promised the long version of every story.
Whoever isn't on watch is going to the caravan's fire tonight. {X_nameDef} says there's salt fish enough to go round, and stories for longer.
{X_nameDef} has asked the colony over to the caravan's fire tonight, and the drivers are already arguing about who tells the first story.

li.label: an evening at the caravan's fire
Buy preserved fare for the stores ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: A share of the caravan's dried and salted fare, at the caravan's price: good for a long winter or a long trip.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} counts out sacks of preserved fare for the colony's stores and the silver into the caravan's chest, and both sides seem pleased with the bargain.
{X_nameDef} counts the silver twice, cheerfully, and sends the drivers over with the sacks.
{X_nameDef} sells the colony enough salted meat and dried fruit for a hard month, and throws in a sack of salt for luck.

li.label: Ask about the roads ahead
li.tip: {A_nameDef} asks the caravan master what the roads are like: who's safe, who's dear, who's hiring. Practice at listening, and the caravan's people think better of the colony for asking.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} spent an hour with {X_nameDef} and a stick drawing roads in the dirt, and came back knowing more about the region than anyone in the colony.
{A_nameDef} sat up late with {X_nameDef} over the caravan's maps, and came back knowing which roads to trust and which to avoid.
{X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} about every town ten days in any direction, and {A_nameDef} remembered as much of it as {A_pronoun} could.

texts.li: [lowtech] Merchants of {FACTION} have come from much further than {FACTION}'s own lands. Their clothes are cut strangely, and their packs smell of spices no one at the colony can name. {X_nameDef}, who speaks for them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} for a few days and show their wares.

[!lowtech] A small trading party of {FACTION} has turned up with crates stamped in alphabets no one here can read, and goods the colony has only ever seen in pictures. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} they're on the way to the far markets and would like to camp {PLACE} for a few days, and trade if anyone's interested.

[ws:fair|ws:trade] With {SITUATION} on, merchants of {FACTION} from the far south have come up the road with rare goods. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few days' camp {PLACE}, to rest and trade on the way.

[lowtech] "May your wells stay sweet and your roofs stay dry." {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} bowed low to {A_nameDef} as {X_pronoun} said it, and then asked, in plainer words, whether the merchants might camp {PLACE} a few days and lay out their wares.

settled.li: The merchants from {FACTION} have laid their wares out on a cloth {PLACE}: little jars, bright cloth, things that tick and things that shine. They've hung a lamp so customers can come after dark.
The merchants' camp {PLACE} has a striped awning over the stall and a smell of strange spices over everything.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who has walked with the merchants {PLACE} all the way from the far south, says {X_pronoun} is tired of roads that go nowhere {X_pronoun} wants to be, and asks whether {X_pronoun} might stay with the colony.
{X_nameDef}, who translates for the merchants {PLACE}, has run out of new words to learn on the road and would like to learn the colony's. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.

farewell.li: The merchants from {FACTION} packed their strange goods and went on toward the far markets, leaving a smell of spice behind for days.
The merchants' camp {PLACE} is gone. {X_nameDef} bowed to the colony's gate before leaving, in some custom of their own.

lines.li: This one is lucky. Very lucky.
We have a saying about that.
Only three of these left in the world.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} spent an evening with {X_nameDef} and came back talking about cities that float, rivers of salt and a king who keeps bees. {A_nameDef} believes about half of it.
[tales] The merchants {PLACE} told the colony stories of the far south over a pot of something very spicy, and {A_nameDef} hasn't stopped talking about it since.
[goods] {X_nameDef} sent a small gift from the merchants' packs to the colony, wrapped in colored cloth, as is their custom with hosts: {THING}.

li.label: Buy their charts and almanacs ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: The merchants carry charts, tables and notes from places nobody here has seen. They will help whoever is studying for the colony.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} sells the colony a bundle of charts and notebooks from the far south, some of them very old. The colony's scholars fall on them.
{X_nameDef} unrolls chart after chart on the colony's table and sells the best of them, with notes in three different hands in the margins.
The merchants part with a crate of notebooks and star tables. {X_nameDef} says one of them was written by a scholar who walked the whole rim.

li.label: Invite them to supper
li.tip: A meal at the colony's table with the merchants as guests: they cook one dish from home, the colony the rest. Recreation, and the merchants warm to the colony.

outcomes.li: The merchants are coming to supper tonight, and {X_nameDef} insists on cooking one dish from home. {X_nameDef} won't say what goes in it.
The merchants will eat at the colony's table tonight. {X_nameDef} has brought a jar of something red and asked for the hottest pan in the kitchen.
Supper with the merchants tonight. {X_nameDef} has asked to help in the kitchen, and the cook hasn't said no yet.

li.label: supper with the merchants

texts.li: Drovers of {FACTION} are walking a herd to market, and the herd is resting in the long grass beyond the ridge while the drovers see about a camp. {X_nameDef}, a lean old drover with a dog that never once took its eyes off {A_nameDef}, asked for leave to camp {PLACE} a few days.

[ws:drove] Another herd is coming past the colony for {SITUATION}. {X_nameDef}, its head drover, asked {A_nameDef} whether {FACTION}'s drovers might camp {PLACE} a few days while the beasts graze beyond the ridge.
[their:grateful] The drovers of {FACTION} know the colony as a friendly stop on the drove road. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, with a nod as if to an old friend, for a few days' camp {PLACE}.

[winter] Drovers of {FACTION}, bringing a late herd down from the high pastures, have asked to camp {PLACE} out of the wind. {X_nameDef} promised {A_nameDef} the herd won't come near the colony's fields.

settled.li: The drovers from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE}, with a rough fence for the dogs and a fire that smells of dung smoke. The herd can be heard beyond the ridge, lowing.
The drovers' camp is up {PLACE}: a fire, a fence, three dogs and not much else. Drovers travel light.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the youngest of the drovers {PLACE}, says {X_pronoun} has had enough of walking behind cows, and asks whether the colony could use someone who knows animals.
{X_nameDef} from the drovers' camp has been helping in the colony's barn every evening, unasked. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether {X_pronoun} might stay and do it for good.

farewell.li: The drovers from {FACTION} moved the herd on at first light. The colony could hear the bells and the dogs long after they'd gone over the ridge.
The drovers' camp {PLACE} is empty, and the grass beyond the ridge is cropped short.

helpTexts.li: [milk] The drovers {PLACE} had more than they could carry, and {X_nameDef} set the rest out at the edge of their camp for the colony: {COUNT} of {THING}.
[milk] {X_nameDef} from the drovers' camp left {COUNT} of {THING} from the herd on the colony's side of the camp, and nodded toward it when a colonist passed.

[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the drovers at their dung-smoke fire and heard about every road, river and bad-tempered bull between here and the market. {A_nameDef} came back smelling of cows and full of stories.

li.label: Buy a beast from the herd ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: One of the drovers' animals, at the drovers' price: young, sound and used to people. It suits the weather here.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} walks a young beast over the ridge on a rope and hands the rope to {A_nameDef}, along with a long list of what it likes and what it doesn't.
{X_nameDef} picks a sound young beast out of the herd and walks it over, and {A_nameDef} is given its rope and its name.
{A_nameDef} chooses a beast from the drovers' herd, and {X_nameDef} spends an hour telling {A_objective} how to keep it content.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} learn herding from them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} spends some hours at the drovers' side, learning how they read a herd. Practice with animals.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going out to the herd with {X_nameDef} for a while, to watch how the drovers do it.
{A_nameDef} is off with the drovers for the day, to learn how {X_nameDef} moves a herd without shouting.
{X_nameDef} has agreed to take {A_nameDef} out with the herd, and says the first lesson is learning to stand still.

texts.li: They came up the road in single file, barefoot and in plain gray, penitents of {FACTION} walking a vow to a shrine far beyond the colony. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, asked {A_nameDef} in a low voice whether they might sleep {PLACE} for a few nights. They ask for nothing else.

[ideology,otherFaith] "We don't keep your faith," {X_nameDef} said, before anything else. The penitents of {IDEO} behind {X_objective} have come from {FACTION} on a long walk of atonement, and {X_pronoun} asked all the same for leave to camp {PLACE}.

[ideology,sameFaith] Penitents of {IDEO}, the colony's own ideoligion, have come up the road walking a vow. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few nights' rest {PLACE}, among people who will understand why they walk.

[meme:Guilty] Every stone in the penitents' packs stands for a wrong they mean to set down at the end of the road. These penitents of {FACTION} came to the colony barefoot, and {X_nameDef} asked to camp {PLACE} for a few nights, promising they would be no trouble to anyone but themselves.

[meme:PainIsVirtue] Penitents of {IDEO} have come up the road with their feet bound in rags and their backs straight. The road is the point, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}; the shrine is only where it ends. They ask to camp {PLACE} a few nights.

[meme:Proselytizer] {X_nameDef} warned {A_nameDef}, with a smile, that the penitents of {IDEO} will talk about their faith to anyone who stands still long enough. Then {X_pronoun} asked for leave to camp {PLACE}.

[ws:sickness] Penitents of {FACTION} are walking to the shrine to pray for the end of {SITUATION}. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether they might rest {PLACE} a few nights, well apart from the colony.

settled.li: The penitents from {FACTION} have made the barest camp the colony has ever seen {PLACE}. There is a fire and a cleared place for prayer, and they sleep on the ground.
[ideology] The penitents of {IDEO} have set out their few holy things on a cloth {PLACE}, and sit before them morning and evening in silence.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the penitents {PLACE}, says {X_possessive} vow ends wherever {X_pronoun} finds a place to make amends with work, and asks whether that might be the colony.
[sameFaith] {X_nameDef} from the penitents' camp says the colony keeps the faith better than the shrine at the end of the road, and asks to stay.

farewell.li: The penitents from {FACTION} went on at dawn, barefoot, without a word. Their camp {PLACE} is swept so clean it's hard to tell anyone was there.
The penitents left before sunrise. {X_nameDef} stopped at the gate to bow, and then they were gone up the road.

helpTexts.li: [blessing] {X_nameDef} and the penitents walked once round the colony at dusk, barefoot, praying for it in voices too low to make out. They didn't ask anyone's leave for it.

[blessing,otherFaith] The penitents prayed for the colony in the way of {IDEO}, at its gate, at dusk. It isn't the colony's ideoligion and the words were strange, but the colonists who heard stood still until they were done.
[blessing,sameFaith] The penitents prayed with the colony this evening, as people of one ideoligion, and {X_nameDef} asked forgiveness for the world in words the colony knows by heart.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with {X_nameDef} at the penitents' fire and asked what they had done to walk so far. {X_nameDef} told {A_objective}. {A_nameDef} has been quiet since.

li.label: Join their evening prayer
li.tip: Whoever wants to goes to the penitents' fire at dusk and sits with them while they pray. Quiet, and something like peace; the penitents are touched.

outcomes.li: Some of the colony are going to sit with the penitents at their evening prayer. {X_nameDef} has made room at the fire.
A few of the colony will kneel with the penitents tonight. {X_nameDef} says anyone is welcome, believer or not.
The penitents have asked the colony to their evening prayer, and {X_nameDef} has laid out mats by the fire.

li.label: evening prayer with the penitents
Give them bread for the road (15 raw food)
li.tip: Food for the rest of their walk. They won't ask for it.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} takes bread and dried fruit to the penitents' camp. {X_nameDef} accepts it with both hands and a bow, and says they will pray for whoever grew it.
{A_nameDef} carries a basket of bread to the penitents, and {X_nameDef} blesses the basket and the one who carried it.
{A_nameDef} brings the penitents food for the road. {X_nameDef} accepts it quietly and asks the colony's name, so they can remember it in their prayers.

texts.li: Pilgrims of {IDEO}, from {FACTION}, have come to the colony's woods. They walk from grove to grove, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, singing to the old trees and listening for what the land wants. They ask to camp {PLACE} for a few days, and promise not to cut a single branch.

[meme:TreeConnection] Tree-singers of {IDEO} have come up the road with their hands stained green and seeds in every pocket. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} there is a tree near the colony they have come a long way to hear, and asked to camp {PLACE} near it.

[meme:Structure_Animist] Everything that grows has a spirit, the pilgrims of {FACTION} believe, and they have come to greet the spirits of the colony's woods. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, very politely, for leave to camp {PLACE} and do it properly.

[sameFaith] Word on the road is that the colony keeps its woods well, and pilgrims of {IDEO}, the colony's own ideoligion, have come to sing to its trees. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} to camp {PLACE} a few days.

settled.li: The tree-singers from {FACTION} have made camp {PLACE} without cutting so much as a twig. They sleep on moss and keep their fire in a ring of old stones, and they pray under the biggest tree.
The tree-singers of {FACTION} have their camp {PLACE}, and have already been round every old tree within sight of it to say good morning.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the tree-singers {PLACE}, says the land here has asked {X_objective} to stay, and {X_pronoun} would like the colony to ask too.

farewell.li: The tree-singers left at dawn, singing, and stopped at the edge of the woods to bow to the trees. They left a ring of planted seeds where their fire had been.
The tree-singers from {FACTION} have gone on to the next grove. {X_nameDef} told the colony its trees are content, which is apparently a compliment.

helpTexts.li: [blessing] The tree-singers went through the colony's fields at dusk, singing to the crops one row at a time. {X_nameDef} says they will grow better for it. The colony's farmers are prepared to believe it.
[blessing,sameFaith] The tree-singers sang with the colony at the old tree this evening, and {A_nameDef} sang the loudest.

[heal] {X_nameDef}, the eldest of the tree-singers, looked at {A_nameDef}'s {THING}, went into the woods, and came back with a leaf to chew and a moss to bind it with. It worked better than anyone expected.
[herbs] The tree-singers {PLACE} gathered more herbs than they need, and left {COUNT} bundles of medicine at the edge of their camp for the colony, each one tied with grass.

li.label: Walk the woods with them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} goes walking with the tree-singers for a few hours, listening. Quiet and calm for {A_objective}; the tree-singers warm to the colony.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} has gone walking in the woods with the tree-singers, to listen to whatever it is they listen to.
{A_nameDef} has gone into the woods with the tree-singers and won't be back before dusk.
The tree-singers have taken {A_nameDef} to the oldest trees nearby, to hear what they call the slow songs.

li.label: Ask them to sing to the fields
li.tip: The tree-singers sing over the colony's growing fields. Practice for the colony's growers, who go along to listen.

outcomes.li: The tree-singers are going out to the colony's fields to sing to the crops, and the growers are going with them.
The tree-singers will walk the colony's rows this afternoon, singing low, and the growers mean to walk with them.
The fields will have singers today. The colony's growers are curious, a little embarrassed, and going anyway.

li.label: the singing in the fields

texts.li: [lowtech] An old healer of {FACTION} has come down the road with a staff, a bag of herbs and an apprentice carrying the rest. {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} {X_pronoun} goes where {X_pronoun} is needed, and asked to camp {PLACE} a few days in case the colony needs {X_objective}.

[!lowtech] A country doctor of {FACTION} has stopped at the colony on a long round of the outlying farms, with a battered bag and a notebook full of other people's coughs. There's room in the notebook for the colony's too, {X_nameDef} says, if the doctor might camp {PLACE} a few days.

[ws:sickness] Every healer in the region is on the road for {SITUATION}, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has stopped at the colony between one bad village and the next. A few days' rest {PLACE} is all {X_nameDef} asks, and anyone ailing can come by while {X_pronoun} is here.

[their:rescued] {X_nameDef}, a healer of {FACTION}, has come out of {X_possessive} way to meet the people who tended {FACTION}'s wounded when no one else would. {X_nameDef} would like to camp {PLACE} a few days, if the colony will have {X_objective}.

settled.li: The healer from {FACTION} has set up {PLACE}, with jars and bundles in rows on a folding table and a bench beside it for anyone who needs looking at.
The healer from {FACTION} has had a kettle on the fire {PLACE} since first light, and a row of jars on the table that gets shorter every day.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, the healer's apprentice, has learned all the road can teach, {X_pronoun} says, and the colony needs a healer more than the road does. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.
{X_nameDef}, the healer {PLACE}, says {X_possessive} knees are tired of roads. If the colony would have an old healer, {X_pronoun} would stay.

farewell.li: The healer from {FACTION} went on to the next village, leaving written instructions behind for nearly every colonist who had sat on the bench.
{X_nameDef}, the traveling healer, has gone. Before leaving, {X_pronoun} looked in on everyone {X_pronoun} had treated, one by one.

lines.li: That's not as bad as it looks.

helpTexts.li: [heal] {X_nameDef}, the traveling healer, sat {A_nameDef} down on the bench and dealt with {A_possessive} {THING} in a quarter of an hour, with a lot of tutting. {A_nameDef} is already feeling better.
[heal,lowtech] {X_nameDef} saw {A_nameDef}'s {THING} from across the yard, came straight over and dealt with it on the spot with a poultice and a bitter tea.
[herbs] {X_nameDef} had more remedies than {X_pronoun} could carry, and left {COUNT} of them for the colony's stores, with instructions written on each one.

li.label: Ask the healer to see {A_nameDef}
li.tip: The travelling healer looks at whoever in the colony is ill or ailing, and does what can be done. It eases it; it doesn't work miracles.

outcomes.li: {X_nameDef} spends an hour with {A_nameDef}, prodding, listening and muttering, and leaves {A_objective} with a remedy and very firm instructions.
{X_nameDef} sits with {A_nameDef} a long while, asks a great many questions, and leaves a bitter tea and stern advice.
{X_nameDef} looks {A_nameDef} over with quick hands and leaves a remedy wrapped in leaves, to be taken exactly as told.

li.label: Pay the healer to teach {A_nameDef} ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: The healer takes the colony's best doctor along on the rounds for a few hours. Practice in medicine, at the healer's side.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going to follow {X_nameDef} about for a few hours and learn what {X_pronoun} can show.
{A_nameDef} will spend the day at {X_nameDef}'s side, watching how the healer works.
{X_nameDef} has agreed to teach {A_nameDef} what can be taught in an afternoon, starting with how to wash hands properly.

texts.li: [lowtech] A band of minstrels of {FACTION} has come up the road with a fiddle, a drum, a hurdy-gurdy and a boy who sings like a bird. {X_nameDef}, who plays the fiddle and does the talking, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might camp {PLACE} a few nights. They play for their supper, and play well.

[!lowtech] A little band of {FACTION}'s musicians has pulled up by the colony in a van painted with stars, guitars and an accordion in the back, and a singer whose cracked voice can quiet a room. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for a few nights' camp {PLACE}. They'll play every evening.

[ws:songs] With {SITUATION} going round the region, every minstrel is on the road, and a band of {FACTION}'s has stopped at the colony. {X_nameDef} swore to {A_nameDef} that they know all the new songs, and asked to camp {PLACE} a few nights.

[their:friend] Minstrels of {FACTION} have come to the colony, and {X_nameDef}, their fiddler, asked for {A_nameDef} by name: there's a song about {A_objective} going round {FACTION}'s towns, and they'd like to play it for {A_objective}. They ask to camp {PLACE} a few nights.

settled.li: The minstrels from {FACTION} have their camp up {PLACE}, with a cleared space before the fire for dancing and their instruments hung from the branches to keep them dry.
The minstrels' camp {PLACE} is never quiet. Someone is always tuning, practicing or arguing about a chord.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, who sings for the minstrels, has sung in every town on the road and wants, just once, to sing in the same place two nights running. {X_nameDef} asks to stay.
{X_nameDef}, who plays the drum for the minstrels, has been drumming on the colony's tables at supper all week. Tonight {X_pronoun} asked whether the colony might want a drummer for good.

farewell.li: The minstrels from {FACTION} went on toward the next town at noon, still playing, with the drum keeping time for the walkers.
The minstrels' camp {PLACE} is empty. Someone at the colony is still humming the last song they played.

lines.li: I'm not flat, the fiddle's sharp.

helpTexts.li: [song] The minstrels {PLACE} played until late tonight, and the music carried all over the colony. {X_nameDef}'s fiddle could be heard from every bed.
[song] The minstrels played the old songs at their fire this evening, the ones everyone knows, and the colony sang along from across the way.
[song,winter] The minstrels played round their fire in the cold tonight, and colonists went out wrapped in blankets to listen, breath steaming.
[tales] {A_nameDef} sat with the minstrels after they'd played and heard a dozen songs that were really news: who married whom, who fought whom, and who was singing about it.

li.label: Hire them to play at a feast ({COUNT} silver)
li.tip: A meal from the colony's stores with the minstrels playing. Recreation for everyone who comes.

outcomes.li: The minstrels are coming to play at the colony's table tonight. {X_nameDef} has already started tuning.
The minstrels will play at the colony's table tonight, and {X_nameDef} has been asking everyone what their favorite song is.
There'll be music at supper. {X_nameDef} has promised something fast for dancing and something slow for after.

li.label: the minstrels' feast
Ask for a song about the colony
li.tip: The minstrels make a song about the colony and sing it at their fire. It will travel with them, and other peoples will hear it.

outcomes.li: The minstrels have been asking questions about the colony all day, and tonight they'll sing what they've made of it at their fire.
The minstrels have gone round the colony collecting stories all day. Tonight, at their fire, they'll sing what they've made of them.
The minstrels are making a song about the colony, and won't say yet whether it's a sad one.

li.label: the colony's song
Have {A_nameDef} learn a tune from them
li.tip: {A_nameDef} sits with the band's best player for a few hours. Practice in the arts.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} is going over to the minstrels' camp to learn a tune or two from {X_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} is off to the minstrels' camp, where {X_nameDef} has promised to teach {A_objective} one tune properly.
{X_nameDef} will teach {A_nameDef} a tune from the road this afternoon, the kind everyone can hum by supper.

texts.li: A slow party of {FACTION} has come up the road behind a covered cart. They are mourners, carrying one of their own home to be buried with their people. {X_nameDef}, who leads them, asked {A_nameDef} whether they might stop {PLACE} for a night or two. They will keep to themselves.

[ws:mourning] There are mourners on every road after {SITUATION}, and a party of them has stopped near the colony. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, in a voice worn thin, for a night or two's camp {PLACE}.

[ws:sickness] The one in the mourners' cart died of {SITUATION}, and the living of {FACTION} walk well apart from it. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for leave to stop {PLACE} a night or two, and swore none of them is sick.

[their:friend] Mourners of {FACTION} have stopped by the colony with their dead. {X_nameDef} asked for {A_nameDef} by name, and said the one they carry spoke of {A_objective} often. They would like to rest {PLACE} a night or two.

[winter] A covered sledge came through the snow this morning, drawn by mourners of {FACTION}. They'd like a sheltered place {PLACE} to stop a night or two, {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, before the last of the road.

[colony:LongMemoried] Mourners of {FACTION} have stopped by the colony with their dead because, {X_nameDef} said, it is a place that remembers. They asked {A_nameDef} whether they might stop {PLACE} a night or two, and say their words where the colony says its own.

settled.li: The mourners from {FACTION} have made a small camp {PLACE}, with the cart drawn up beside the fire and a lamp beside the cart that is never let go out.
The mourners' camp is up {PLACE}. Someone sits by the covered cart at every hour, day and night.

joinTexts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the mourners {PLACE}, says there's nothing left at home now but the grave they're carrying their dead to, and the others can see it filled without {X_objective}. {X_nameDef} asks whether there might be a place here.
{X_nameDef}, who has sat by the cart {PLACE} every night, says the one they carry always meant to settle somewhere like this. {X_nameDef} would like to do it for them, if the colony will allow it.

farewell.li: The mourners from {FACTION} went on at first light with their cart, walking slowly, the lamp still lit beside it.
The mourners' camp {PLACE} is empty. {X_nameDef} left a sprig of green on the colony's gatepost, as {FACTION} do for those who let the dead rest a while.

lines.li: He always took the long way.
We'll sing for him at home.

helpTexts.li: [tales] {A_nameDef} sat a while at the mourners' fire, and {X_nameDef} told {A_objective} about the one they're carrying home: who they were, what they loved, what they used to say. {A_nameDef} came back very quiet.
[tales] The mourners told {A_nameDef} the story of the one in the cart, start to finish, over a long evening. By the end {A_nameDef} felt {A_pronoun} had known them.

li.label: Sit vigil with them tonight
li.tip: {A_nameDef} goes to sit with the mourners at their fire through the night hours. A kindness they will remember.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} will go and sit vigil with the mourners tonight. {X_nameDef} said they'd keep a place by the lamp.
{A_nameDef} will sit up with the mourners tonight. {X_nameDef} has put aside a blanket and a place by the lamp.
{A_nameDef} is going to keep the mourners company through the night, and {X_nameDef} said it was more than they'd hoped for.

li.label: Stand by the road when they go
li.tip: The colony stands bareheaded by the road while the mourners carry their dead past. Among many peoples, that is a great kindness.

outcomes.li: The colony will stand by the road when the mourners go on. {X_nameDef} thanked {A_nameDef} without words.
When the mourners leave, the colony will line the road in silence. {X_nameDef} pressed {A_nameDef}'s hand when told.
The colony will see the mourners off at the road. {X_nameDef} said it was the kindest thing anyone had offered them.

li.label: standing by the road for the mourners
Give them food for the road (15 raw food)
li.tip: Food for the rest of their journey home.

outcomes.li: {A_nameDef} takes food to the mourners' camp. {X_nameDef} takes it with a nod and says the one in the cart would have thanked the colony with a song.
{A_nameDef} brings the mourners food for the road, and {X_nameDef} gives thanks for the living and for the one in the cart.
{A_nameDef} carries food to the mourners' camp. {X_nameDef} says it will last them to the next town, and further.
